failure.stage: carry the teapot upright over the mug

rounds.diagnosis: The transport goal put teapot.spout_tip only in contact-level standoff (0-2 cm) above mug.opening_center; with the spout tip that low the pot's body and handle sit at or below the mug rim (handle_center is 2.7 cm below the opening plane), so every candidate goal pose collided with the mug and no collision-free goal existed, and the pour stage's identical contact band left no room for the body to swing through the 90 deg tilt. Stepping the above-terms from contact to small clearance lifts the band away from the rim while keeping its height, giving collision-free poses for the hover goal and the tilt sweep; the pour path and pour subgoal bands are stepped together so the pour stage still accepts the raised transport goal as its start and contains its own subgoal. All other rows (upright path, centering on the opening, the antiparallel spout direction) are untouched, so the pour still lands in the mug.

failure.stage: carry the teapot upright over the mug
failure.message: no transport goal is a start the pour accepts

rounds.diagnosis: The standoff over the mug was too low. With clearance 'small' the spout tip sits only ~2 cm above mug.opening_center while the teapot body/handle extends ~21 cm horizontally at the upright goal and the pot swings through a wide arc during the tilt, so the pot body fouls the mug rim: no collision-free goal exists for the carry stage and the pour path has no room to rotate. Stepping the above-mug clearance from small to medium on the carry subgoal lifts the whole band away from the rim (as the stage goal itself asks, 'a standoff that keeps the pot's body clear of the mug's rim'), and the matching step on the pour stage's path and subgoal keeps the pour band aligned with the new carry goal so the tilt still starts where the carry ends and still pours into the mug.
